newsitem.title: USA: Florida has sold some 80 percent of tobacco holdings.
newsitem.headline: Florida has sold some 80 percent of tobacco holdings.

text.p: Florida sold nearly $650 million in cigarette company stock in a little over three weeks last month after the state decided to dump tobacco from its pension plan portfolio, state officials said Monday.

Officials in Florida, one of many states waging legal battles against the tobacco industry, voted in May to jettison the highly profitable cigarette component of the state's $69 billion employee pension fund.

By Monday, nearly 78 percent of the tobacco portfolio had been sold, said Tom Herndon, executive director of the Florida Department of Administration. About $185 million in tobacco company stock remained in the fund, he said.

Florida sold about 16 million shares of stock, including 10.6 million shares of Philip Morris Cos. Inc., between May 30 and June 20, when a proposed national settlement was announced between tobacco companies and 40 states, including Florida.
Herndon added, however, that the portfolio's managers decided to stop divesting cigarette companies after their stock prices dropped following the settlement announcement.
